entries.title: II Samuel 22:1
segments: Deliverance from trouble should be ever followed by devout acknowledgment of God as its author, and hearty thanksgiving for his mercies.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:2
segments: Rock, and--fortress; support and protection.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:3
segments: The God of my rock;

Shield; defence from enemies. 
 
  Horn; the emblem of power. 
 
  Tower; source of security.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:4
segments: Humble dependence on God with believing supplication to him for all which is needed, is one of the best means of gaining benefit from trials while they last, and in due time a glorious deliverance from them.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:5
segments:
Waves of death; calamities breaking in upon him like the waves of the sea, and threatening to destroy him. 
 
  Floods of ungodly men; this figure expresses both their multitude and their impetuous force.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:6
segments: Prevented; this word originally meant, to go before, so as to stop one's way.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:8
segments:
vv 8-16. 
 
A highly poetical description of God's appearing for the deliverance of his servant, and the destruction of his enemies. 
 
All created things are dependent upon and under the control of Jehovah, and whenever he sees best he can use them as instruments for the salvation of his friends and the destruction of his enemies.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:13
segments: Through the brightness--kindled; or, from the brightness that was before him burning coals proceeded.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:16
segments: Channels--appeared, the foundations of the world were discovered; the waters are represented as fleeing at God's presence, so that the deep channels of the sea are laid bare to human vision.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:17
segments: Many waters; great afflictions.  See note to

entries.title: II Samuel 22:19
segments: Prevented; see note to

entries.title: II Samuel 22:20
segments: Into a large place; where I had freedom from my enemies and the distresses they brought upon me.  The figure is taken from military life, where nothing is so dangerous as to be hemmed in among narrow defiles.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:21
segments:
Righteousness--cleanness of my hands; his innocence of the sins charged upon him, and his hearty devotion to the service of God. 
 
The Lord often treats men in this world according to their character; and he will always do it in the world to come.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:24
segments:
Upright; honest, sincere, and merciful. 
 
  Mine iniquity; that to which he was most tempted.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:27
segments: Show thyself unsavory; he would contend with, oppose, and punish them.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:28
segments: The humble, sincere, and benevolent are objects of God's favor, and receive special tokens of his love; while the proud, hypocritical, and selfish he abhors, and will visit with his displeasure.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:29
segments: My lamp; showing him the way in which he should go.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:30
segments:
Run through; broken. 
 
  Leaped over a wall; scaled the wall of the enemy.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:34
segments:
Like hinds' feet; very swift, and able to stand in safety on the most dangerous places. 
 
There are no difficulties in the path of duty which those who trust in God may not overcome, and no dangers which they may not escape.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:35
segments: A bow of steel is broken; or, according to some translators, is bent; showing that God had given him great strength.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:36
segments: Gentleness; condescending kindness and teaching.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:37
segments: Enlarged my steps; given me full liberty and enabled me to walk in safety.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:40
segments: God adapts his dealings to the circumstances of his people, and gives mercies according to their necessities; so that as their day is, their wisdom, strength, consolation, and all needful blessings will be.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:41
segments: The necks of mine enemies; the meaning of the original is, Thou hast caused mine enemies to turn their backs before me.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:42
segments: Answered them not; their cry to him was that of distress merely, after they were given up to ruin as a punishment for their sins.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:45
segments: From what God has done for his people they are encouraged as to what he will do, and led confidently to expect that he will fulfil his promises for ever.

entries.title: II Samuel 22:46
segments: Shall be afraid out of their close places; shall come forth out of them with fear.
